dedupe_keys.name: european flood awareness system efas river discharge historical simulations forecasts reforecasts and seasonal forecasts

description: EFAS is the European flood forecasting system of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service. Its datasets are gridded outputs of the open-source LISFLOOD hydrological model at 1 arcminute resolution (about 1.5 km at European latitudes; 5 km in version 4.0 and older). Coverage: the EFAS domain over Europe; the historical simulation, forced with gridded observed precipitation and temperature, runs from 1991 to the present; medium-range forecasts, initialised twice daily with 5- to 15-day lead times from ECMWF high-resolution and 51-member ensemble, DWD and 20-member COSMO-LEPS forcing, run from October 2018; reforecasts give 20 years initialised twice weekly; seasonal forecasts are initialised monthly from November 2020. Variables are river discharge, volumetric soil moisture, snow water equivalent, root-zone soil wetness index and runoff, with auxiliary upstream area, elevation, soil depth, wilting capacity and field capacity. Format and access: free download from the Early Warning Data Store after registration, via web form or API. Licence: CEMS-FLOODS datasets licence (PDF linked from each dataset). Caveats: forecasts are released to the public with a 30-day delay and real-time data go only to EFAS partners; version changes alter resolution and time step. Simulation uses: river discharge and soil moisture series for flood hazard exposure of bridges, roads, rail and utilities, emergency response planning and climate adaptation. Related records: the global counterpart GloFAS (data-glofas) and the Copernicus ground motion service (data-copernicus-european-ground-motion-service).
